title: Archived-artifact rule now excludes any top-level review-* directory, which can hide real source changes

finding.claim: Archived-artifact rule now excludes any top-level review-* directory, which can hide real source changes
finding.evidence: The new rule treats any path under a top-level directory starting with review- or review_ as archived output, regardless of whether it is actually generated review data.
finding.recommendation: Narrow the exclusion to known generated-output locations or require an explicit marker file/schema before classifying a directory as archived. Do not blanket-exclude all top-level review-* and review_* paths.

probe.summary: Archived-rule probe (`probes/closingA_archived_rule.py`): `_archived_rule` (core.py:165) behaves exactly as its docstring states — a top-level `review-*`/`review_*` directory classifies as archived (`review-tools/real_source.py` → 'review-*/'), nested review dirs do NOT (`docs/review-v15/out.json` → None), and `gate-attempts.*` matches by basename anywhere. Two facts bound the harm: (1) this repository has no top-level review-* SOURCE directory — every such directory is run-record output, which is what the rule exists to classify; (2) classification is not deletion: archived-text findings are preserved in the record's archived_text_findings, visible to any reader. The 'hide real source changes' scenario requires a future top-level source directory named review-* — a layout that does not exist here.
